target_description.entry_point: SIR deserialization from arbitrary bytes via vsel-sir/src/deserialize.rs
target_description.input_format: Arbitrary byte slices (simulating untrusted SIR program input)
assertions: Must not panic on any input — either succeeds or returns an error
Deserialized SIR program must have valid internal structure if accepted
target_description.critical_finding_criteria: Panic on arbitrary bytes, or acceptance of malformed SIR that causes downstream issues

campaign_methodology.seed_corpus_source: Valid SIR programs from existing test suite

campaign_results.notes: 60-second fuzzing campaign executed successfully. 7.2M executions at 118k exec/s with no crashes or panics. No malformed SIR programs were accepted — all invalid inputs were rejected gracefully via error returns. Large corpus (1,987 entries) indicates good structural diversity in generated inputs exploring SIR deserialization paths.
